newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU concerned by torture reports at Kosovo trial.
newsitem.headline: EU concerned by torture reports at Kosovo trial.

text.p: The European Union said on Wednesday it was alarmed at reports that 20 ethnic Albanians convicted of terrorism in the Serbian province of Kosovo last month had been tortured.

"The EU is extremely concerned about reports that the accused have been tortured and about the non-respect of principles of the rule of law," it said in a statement released by the Dutch government, current holders of the EU presidency.
In particular, the EU said it was worried that defendants were repeatedly denied access to lawyers and sentences were mainly based on self-incriminatory evidence.
"It is of grave concern that the court refused to follow up statements that their self-incriminatory confessions had been extracted under duress," it said.
It called on the Serbian authorities to allow the United Nations to study the case, taking into account the criticism raised against the court and the police.
The 20 Albanians received a total of 107 years in prison on convictions for association for the purpose of hostile activity, threatening territorial integrity, and terrorism.
Earlier this month, the United States' State Department said the trial was "marred by a number of serious judicial irregularities".

Ethnic Albanians outnumber Serbs by nine to one in Kosovo, where around 30 people have been killed in guerrilla violence over the past year. A crackdown by police in January resulted in the arrest of some 70 people.
